summary: Braised baby artichokes with fennel and cherry tomatoes: artichoke quarters seared about 5 minutes in olive oil with garlic, then braised covered about 15 minutes with fennel, tomatoes, rosemary, white wine and lemon; serves 2 as a hearty side or as a condiment for pasta, polenta or risotto.
glance: 2 as a hearty side dish or pasta condiment
8 baby, trimmed, quartered and kept in lemon water
sear about 5 minutes, braise covered about 15 minutes until fully tender
yield: 2 as a hearty side dish or pasta condiment
faq: Why braise baby artichokes?
They love being braised: it develops multiple levels of flavor, the browned flavors from an initial sear, the mellow sweetness of the tender heart, and slow infusion with aromatics.
How do I trim baby artichokes?

Fill a bowl with water and the juice of 1 lemon. Trim off the upper half of each artichoke, break off the tough outer leaves and cut off their base, trim and peel the stem, quarter lengthwise and cut out the hairy choke, tossing each quarter into the acidulated water right away.
How much of the artichoke do I throw away?

A lot; be a little ruthless and you'll be rewarded with a tender, delicious heart, stem and a few leaves. The author's first chef told him he was being "too nice to the vegetables": the best way to honor them is to trim away the less edible parts.
Can I change the vegetables and flavors?

Add black or green olives, lemon zest or Parmigiano-Reggiano (if not vegan); peas or fresh fava beans can replace or augment the fennel. If the fennel is full-sized, cut it into 2-inch by 1/3-inch batons.
How do I serve it?
As a course by itself, a side dish, or better, as a condiment for pasta, polenta or risotto.

summary: Super spicy tofu and peppers, or mild if you prefer: extra-firm tofu cubes fried 3 minutes, then jalapeno (treated as a vegetable), bell pepper and scallions stir-fried about 1 minute until the colors brighten and tossed 30 seconds with a tamari, garlic and sesame sauce; serves 2.
glance: 4 jalapenos; use all red bell pepper for a mild, kid-friendly version
1/2 pound extra-firm, 1/2-inch cubes, patted dry and fried about 3 minutes
about 1 minute until the colors brighten, then 30 seconds with the sauce
Vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and kosher (with gluten-free tamari)
faq: How do I make it mild?
The jalapeno is treated like a vegetable, not just a flavoring, so you adjust the ratio of jalapeno to red bell pepper. Using 100% bell pepper gives a dish friendly to kids and the heat-averse.
Why do colors brighten when stir-frying peppers?
It's a good sign they are at the crisp-tender point: the air and water trapped between the translucent skin and the brightly colored flesh cook out, allowing the flesh to shine through.
Why prepare everything first?
Like any stir-fry, have the sauce mixed and all of the tofu and vegetables cut before you start, because once the tofu hits the pan the dish comes together fast.
What can I add?
Roasted peanuts for another layer of flavor and crunch, or a few pinches of ground Szechwan peppercorn for its tongue-numbing tingle.
How do I get the tofu to brown?
Pat it dry on a clean absorbent towel in a single layer, pat it dry once more, and fry in a single layer in a very hot cast iron skillet or wok, tossing occasionally until golden brown.

summary: Farro with collard greens and bacon salt: tender farro stirred with chickpeas, topped with collards cooked down with onion, garlic and chili flakes and tossed with olive oil and bacon salt (or salt and smoked paprika); serves 4 as a one-pot meal.
glance: cooked per package directions until tender but not falling apart (a pearled farro from Italy)
3 big bunches collards or other strong greens (not spinach), cooked until very tender
1 teaspoon bacon salt, or regular salt with smoked paprika
Vegetarian; not vegan (the bacon salt contains milk products)
faq: Is Bacon Salt vegetarian?

The author didn't know until a friend brought some to a blogger get-together; it's a vegetarian product, as processed bacon bits are a soy product too. This recipe is vegetarian but not vegan because the bacon salt contains milk products. You can use regular salt and smoked paprika instead.
What is farro?
A very ancient whole grain, one of the staples of the Roman poor, with a flavor the author finds somewhere between wheat and barley. It's a nice change of pace from rice and couscous.
How do I cook farro?

Cook according to the package directions: there are different types with different cooking times. Cook until tender but not falling apart, drain, and stir in chickpeas. The author suggests cooking six servings because serving sizes are always too small.
How do I cook the collards?

Fry the onion in olive oil, add chili flakes and garlic for 20 seconds, then add the greens and a splash of water if they aren't wet, cover, reduce the heat after a minute or two and stir occasionally until very thoroughly tender and wilted. Drain the excess water.
Why collards with a smoky seasoning?
Greens are often cooked with pork in both the American South and in Italy; the smoky bacon salt brings that flavor.

summary: Grapefruit and avocado salad: grapefruit supremes cut with a clean in-and-back technique, cubed avocado and paper-thin red onion dressed with grapefruit juice, olive oil, salt and Dijon shaken in a jar and finished with black salt; serves 2.
glance: 1/4 cup grapefruit juice, 1/4 cup olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon Dijon
cut grapefruit supremes over a bowl to catch the juice
faq: What are citrus supremes?

Clean segments of citrus fruit without membrane or pith. The author learned from Chef Janine at Cafe Flora: instead of cutting on both sides of the membrane, go in on one side, flip your knife around and come back toward you on the other side, maybe leaving a bit of flesh behind. You end up with clean segments and a beautiful cup of juice.
What do I do with the leftover juice?
Squeeze the leftover bits of grapefruit and the juice gathered while cutting, measure 1/4 cup for the dressing and drink the rest as a cook's treat.
How do I make the dressing?

Shake 1/4 cup grapefruit juice with the olive oil, kosher salt and mustard in a jar to emulsify, add a little good vinegar if it needs more acidity, and leave it underseasoned so you can finish with black salt.
What variations work?
Different citrus (blood oranges!), feta and/or cilantro. Etta's has a famous crabmeat version, and Cafe Flora does one with shiitake mushrooms and a ginger-miso dressing on greens.
How do I serve it?
Arrange the grapefruit, avocado and onion on a plate and drizzle on the dressing just before serving, with black salt and black pepper.

summary: No-churn chocolate ice cream, an experiment: chocolate, cream and milk heated to 190°F and blended with cocoa, sugar and 1.6 grams of LM pectin (about 0.23%) into a base poured into a chilled shallow pan and frozen a couple of hours with no churning and no ice crystals; yields 1 pint plus.
glance: 1.6 grams Pomona LM pectin, about 0.23% of the mix by weight
in a chilled shallow 9x13 pan; soften 10 minutes before serving
faq: How can ice cream be made without churning?

The primary purpose of churning is to keep ice crystals small while freezing; pectin solves that a different way by creating a light but fine gel matrix that limits how large the ice crystals can grow. The author was inspired by a jelly ice cream whose pectin prevented large crystals.
Why use LM pectin and so little of it?

LM pectin sets in the presence of calcium, which dairy has a lot of (unlike traditional HM pectin, which sets with sugar). The author's first try at 1% by weight was very gummy with weak flavor and poor melt; about 0.23% was drastically better, with a hint of pudding-pop but creamy and free of ice crystals.
How do I make the base?

Heat the cream, milk and chopped chocolate to a bare simmer (190°F), use an immersion blender to form a vortex, slowly pour in the dry mixture of cocoa, sugar, salt and pectin, and blend a full minute more; then strain into a chilled shallow pan, cover and freeze.
Is this a finished recipe?

It's experimental: the author made it only twice and lists open questions, such as how long it keeps, whether even less pectin works, whether stirring in the freezer helps, and how it works with other flavors or larger batches.
How do I blend the hot liquid safely?
An immersion blender is used; a regular blender works only if you know the method for blending hot liquids safely.

summary: Chilled tomato buttermilk soup: 2 1/2 cups cold buttermilk blended for at least a minute with 32 tomato confit halves and salt, strained and served in chilled bowls with chopped confit, chives, olive oil and flaky salt; serves 4 in 10 minutes if the confit is already made.
glance: 10 minutes, with tomato confit already made
2 1/2 cups cold buttermilk and 32 tomato confit halves (36 total)
faq: What do I need to make this soup?
Tomato confit already made: the concentrated tomatoes turn the buttermilk a beautiful pink color, making the soup criminally easy and refreshingly tart.
How do I get a smooth soup?
Puree the buttermilk, 32 confit halves and the salt in a blender or with an immersion blender for at least a minute, then strain. Garnish with the 4 remaining chopped halves.
What if the buttermilk is too thick or sour?
Taste your buttermilk first. If it's too thick or too sour, dilute it with up to 2/3 cup of milk.
Can I make it vegan?
Use part vegan sour cream and part soy, rice or hemp milk in place of the buttermilk.
What variations work?
A little lemon zest in the puree; cherry tomato halves or diced cucumber to garnish instead of confit; tiny leaves of oregano or thyme instead of chives.

summary: A guest post from Yu Ching of Lemonpi: jackfruit brown sugar upside-down cake, based on a Joanne Chang recipe from Flour. Canned jackfruit set in a caramel with tamarind, covered with a brown sugar and melted butter batter and baked 45 minutes at 350°F in a 9-inch pan.
glance: 350°F (175°C) for about 45 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean
at least 30 minutes in the pan before inverting
one 440-gram can ripe jackfruit in syrup, drained and halved
faq: Do I have to use canned jackfruit?
The recipe calls for tinned ripe jackfruit mostly for convenience. If you have fresh jackfruit readily available, use it. The topping would also work with sliced bananas or even mango.
How do I make the caramel?

Cook 100 grams of sugar to a medium golden brown caramel over medium heat, carefully whisk in 6 tablespoons of soft butter and then the optional tamarind puree (it will splutter), bring to a boil, whisking to emulsify, and pour into the buttered pan to just cover the base.
How do I unmold an upside-down cake?

Once baked and cooled at least 30 minutes, slip a paring knife around the edges to loosen it, then boldly upend it onto a plate and remove the tin with a flourish. Yu Ching says the great reveal is part of the pleasure.
Who is Yu Ching?
The writer of the Lemonpi blog, known for original desserts like a parsnip and cocoa nib cake and classics like gateau Breton.
How should I serve it?
Warm or at room temperature.

summary: Chili borracho ("drunken chili"): pinto, black and kidney beans with dark beer, dried chiles, ancho powder and unsweetened cocoa, pressure-cooked 33 minutes (or simmered from precooked beans for 30), with the cooking liquid reduced to a thick sauce; serves 3-4 in about 1 hour.
glance: 3 as a one-pot meal or 4 with cornbread and guacamole
1 cup pinto, 1 cup black, 2/3 cup kidney, cooked from dried
one 12-ounce very dark beer, 2 dried chile negro, cocoa, cinnamon
Vegan if you choose vegan garnishes
yield: 3 as a one-pot meal or 4 with cornbread and guacamole
faq: What makes this chili different?

The author isn't a believer in lots of vegetables or grains in chili: it's all about the beans, complemented by a savory sauce and lots of tasty garnish. Dark beer, dried chiles and unsweetened cocoa powder create the deep bass notes, reminiscent of Oaxacan mole.
Why a pressure cooker?

It's the author's favorite way to make chili: it cooks the beans from scratch and includes the bean cooking liquid as part of the broth. The cooker needs about 8 cups of liquid per pound of beans (check your manual), which would be a soup, so you drain off the sauce and simmer it down to about 1 cup, then add it back.
Can I make it without a pressure cooker?
Yes: use precooked beans, skip the water, and simmer for 30 minutes with the other ingredients.
Can I make it ahead?
If you have the time, make it a couple of hours in advance or even the day before; the flavors only get better with rest.
What garnishes go on top?
Sour cream, minced onion, shredded cheddar, minced cilantro or parsley and hot sauce, passed so each diner customizes.

summary: Fresh fettuccine with broccoli raab in a light, buttery tomato sauce: tomato juice, white wine and lemon emulsified with butter (a "beurre rouge") that coats the noodles without overwhelming them, tossed with blanched broccoli raab and parmigiano; serves 3-4 in 30 minutes.
glance: butter emulsified with tomato juice, then tomatoes, 1/2 cup wine and lemon, reduced to coat a spoon
faq: Why a light sauce for fresh pasta?

Fresh pasta doesn't generally enjoy a full-bodied tomato "gravy" like dried spaghetti. A much lighter broth of tomato juice, white wine and lemon, emulsified with butter, coats the noodles without overwhelming their delicate flavor.
How do I emulsify the sauce?

Whisk the butter and onions while drizzling in the juice from the tomato can, as in a beurre blanc (here a beurre rouge). If it gives you trouble, whisk in a little more cold butter. Don't burn the butter.
Can I use other vegetables?
If you don't have broccoli raab, zucchini or summer squash would work; fresh basil is a delicious addition.
What can I use instead of white wine?
Dry vermouth, which the author always has on hand because it keeps pretty well and he loves the flavor.
How do I assemble the dish?

Boil the raab until tender and shock it in ice water; when nearly ready to serve, reheat it in the sauce, cook the pasta, and toss it in the skillet with the sauce, 1/4 cup wine, half the cheese and pepper. Serve on a preheated platter with the remaining sauce poured over.

summary: Tofu and kimchi dinner for one in under ten minutes and one cast iron pan: extra-firm tofu fried in a very hot skillet until golden, a bit of onion and ginger for 30 seconds, then mounded in a bowl with sesame oil, scallions, sesame seeds, vegetarian kimchi and ssamjang or another chile sauce.
glance: 1 tablespoon ssamjang, or 1 teaspoon kochujang or sriracha
faq: Is vegetarian kimchi hard to find?

It can be a little hard: look closely at the ingredients for shrimp paste and similar. The author likes Dae Han Tofu Company's, and in Seattle the non-traditional Firefly Kitchens booth at the farmer's markets.
How do I get the tofu golden?
Heat a large cast iron skillet over a very high flame, add the oil, and 5 seconds later the tofu with a great big pinch of salt. Fry, tossing occasionally, until golden brown.
What is ssamjang?
A Korean condiment the author loves because it is only moderately spicy with a lot of flavor complexity, so you can use quite a bit. Kochujang or sriracha can be used instead.
How can I embellish it?
Sauteed shiitakes, finely shredded nori, a fried egg or a handful of sugar snap peas. The author didn't even make rice, but you might like some.
Can I make it for company?
Yes, multiply as needed.
